title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO Following White House Intervention
summary: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and director eleven days after his resignation, following intervention from President Donald Trump. The move sent Nvidia shares surging roughly 33%, rebounding from a sharp sell-off triggered by his departure.
popularity_basis: Dominated global financial and technology headlines due to Nvidia's market dominance, geopolitical implications, and a massive single-day stock rebound.

title: CrowdStrike Agrees to Acquire Zscaler in $43.9 Billion All-Stock Deal
summary: Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike signed a definitive agreement to acquire cloud security provider Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock transaction. The deal aims to unite endpoint and zero-trust network security for enterprise and AI workloads, though CrowdStrike shares fell amid investor concerns over dilution and integration.
popularity_basis: One of the largest acquisitions in cybersecurity history, drawing heavy coverage across enterprise tech and Wall Street outlets.

title: Virginia and Oregon Sue SpaceX Over Grok AI Sexualized Deepfakes
summary: Attorneys general in Virginia and Oregon filed separate consumer protection lawsuits against SpaceX and subsidiary X Corp., alleging the Grok AI chatbot generated nonconsensual sexualized images, including child sexual abuse material. They are the first US states to sue over Grok's image-generation safeguards.
popularity_basis: First state-level enforcement lawsuits targeting SpaceX over xAI's Grok, carrying major legal and AI safety implications.

title: OpenAI Chief Scientist Urges Industry-Wide AI Development Limits Using Perplexity
summary: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki proposed that rival frontier AI labs adopt shared development limits tied partly to model perplexity metrics before recursive self-improvement accelerates in 2027. CEO Sam Altman endorsed the call, though no major competitors have publicly agreed to the framework.
popularity_basis: High-profile safety proposal from OpenAI leadership sparking widespread debate across AI labs and policymakers.

title: Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang Warns Superintelligence Is Arriving
summary: Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang warned that artificial superintelligence is arriving and urged the industry to deviate from its default trajectory to preserve human agency. His remarks followed claims that an Anthropic researcher used Claude to help solve the Riemann hypothesis.
popularity_basis: Broad international coverage driven by senior Big Tech executive warnings tied to recent AI mathematical breakthroughs.

title: OpenAI and Cisco Launch Open-Source Shirudo Runtime for Live Linux Security
summary: OpenAI and Cisco unveiled Shirudo, an open-source eBPF security runtime that allows operators to test and deploy temporary exploit shields on running Linux systems without waiting for patches or reboots. The tool uses hardware-backed TPM verification to audit active protections.
popularity_basis: Major joint open-source security release combining OpenAI's frontier research with Cisco's enterprise infrastructure.

title: Dragos Exposes Undetected Hacks and Prompt Theft at AI Inference Providers
summary: Cybersecurity firm Dragos revealed that attackers breached at least three AI inference providers and stole customer prompts—including data flagged for zero data retention—without being detected. Researchers uncovered the intrusions by seeding nearly two million API prompts with canary traps.
popularity_basis: Significant enterprise security impact exposing privacy gaps across third-party AI model routing and inference APIs.

title: Hackers Exploited Microsoft Entra Connect Health Flaw to Harvest Admin Emails
summary: Microsoft notified customers that attackers exploited an API vulnerability in Entra Connect Health between July and November 2026 to read administrator email addresses and tenant configuration metadata. While passwords and tokens were not exposed, security experts warn the data enables highly targeted spear-phishing.
popularity_basis: Widespread enterprise relevance affecting hybrid cloud identity administrators across Microsoft's ecosystem.

title: Human Security Disrupts BadBox 3.0 Ad Fraud and Proxy Botnet
summary: Human Security reported disrupting BadBox 3.0, a massive malware operation infecting low-cost uncertified Android TV boxes and devices to generate 40 billion daily ad bid requests. The campaign also covertly enrolled victims' home connections into eleven residential proxy networks.
popularity_basis: Record-scale botnet disruption affecting global digital advertising infrastructure and consumer IoT hardware.

title: UK NHS Launches World's Largest AI Breast Cancer Screening Trial
summary: The UK National Health Service opened recruitment for the EDITH trial, deploying AI-assisted mammogram reading across 30 sites for nearly 700,000 women. The three-year study tests whether AI can detect cancers earlier while easing severe radiologist workforce shortages.
popularity_basis: Landmark real-world clinical deployment of medical AI at national healthcare scale.

title: AI Inference Startup Marlowe Raises $277 Million Seed at $1.15 Billion Valuation
summary: Six-month-old startup Marlowe raised a $277 million seed round led by Accel at a $1.15 billion valuation to build AI inference factories using AMD and Etched chips. Founded by former Microsoft executives, the company aims to lower inference costs outside Nvidia's ecosystem.
popularity_basis: Massive seed valuation underscoring intense venture appetite for non-Nvidia AI inference infrastructure.

title: GL.iNet Cloud Flaw Exploited to Plant Malware on Routers and KVM Devices
summary: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote management service to install malware and root shells on consumer routers and KVM devices. Investigators also uncovered an unrelated, older backdoor on dozens of managed devices and urged immediate firmware updates.
popularity_basis: Active exploitation of widely used travel routers and remote KVM hardware requiring urgent user remediation.

title: Autonomous Hacking Framework ARTEX Continues Spreading on GitHub Despite Takedown
summary: Forks of ARTEX, an open-source Go framework that connects large language models to autonomous hacking subagents, remain active on GitHub despite the original author pulling the repository. Security researchers and the FBI warn the tool is being used to attack organizations at machine speed.
popularity_basis: High security community interest in the proliferation of LLM-driven offensive cyber tooling.

title: Raimondo-Led Report Finds AI-Heavy Sectors Cut Early-Career Hiring by 3% to 8%
summary: A joint RAISE US and Burning Glass study led by former Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo found that early-career job postings in AI-intensive industries fell 3% to 8% between 2021 and 2026. The report warns that non-degree workers face over 80% of automation exposure.
popularity_basis: Empirical workforce data quantifying AI's impact on entry-level hiring across major industries.

title: Elsevier and IEEE Investigate AI Papers Claiming Fingerprint Blood-Type Prediction
summary: Academic publishers Elsevier and IEEE opened formal ethics investigations into over a dozen peer-reviewed papers claiming AI models predict human blood types from fingerprints with over 90% accuracy. Forensic audits traced the datasets to unlabelled SOCOFing fingerprint images arbitrarily sorted into folders.
popularity_basis: Significant academic integrity scandal highlighting peer-review failures in applied machine learning research.

title: Trump Formally Nominates Kirsten Davies as US National Cyber Director
summary: President Donald Trump formally moved to nominate former Defense Department CIO Kirsten Davies as permanent US National Cyber Director following broad industry support. Davies, currently serving as acting director, pledges to modernize critical national infrastructure and expand cyber talent.
popularity_basis: Key US federal cybersecurity leadership development shaping national cyber policy.

title: Community Backlash Mounts Against Big Tech AI Data Centers Over Power and Water
summary: Local opposition to hyperscale AI data centers is intensifying globally, with hundreds of objections filed against an Anthropic-anchored project in Australia and protests over a planned facility in London's Brick Lane. Residents cite strain on power grids, water supplies, and housing.
popularity_basis: Growing global infrastructure bottleneck affecting AI expansion plans for Microsoft, Amazon, OpenAI, and Anthropic.
